page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn5i-c28g1.14xlarge is a GPU-accelerated virtual machine instance within the ecs.gn5i family powered by KVM hypervisor technology. The instance features 56 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs paired with 224.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a 1:4 CPU-to-RAM ratio of 4.0 GB per core. Network connectivity provides a baseline bandwidth of 10 Gbps, and no complimentary public IPv4 addresses or local disk storage are included, requiring external cloud block storage for persistent data.

Hardware acceleration is supplied by two embedded NVIDIA P4 GPUs delivering a combined 16 GB of video memory. The inclusion of dual NVIDIA P4 graphics processors positions this instance for AI inference workloads, media processing, and light graphics rendering. From a resource density perspective, the P4 accelerator provides energy-efficient compute capability relative to large training GPUs, offering a balanced allocation of parallel processing cores alongside dedicated host vCPU capacity.

The allocation of 56 vCPUs alongside 224 GB of host RAM and 10 Gbps network throughput makes the ecs.gn5i-c28g1.14xlarge suitable for concurrent deep learning inference serving, real-time video encoding, and data preprocessing tasks.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.gn5i-c28g1.14xlarge is a GPU-accelerated cloud instance engineered for AI inference and parallel compute tasks. Built on x86_64 architecture using the KVM hypervisor, this instance supplies 56 dedicated vCPUs and 224.0 GB of RAM, yielding 4.0 GB of memory per core. Hardware acceleration is delivered via two NVIDIA P4 GPUs providing 16 GB of aggregate VRAM. Networking features a 10 Gbps baseline bandwidth. The instance lacks local disk storage, necessitating attachment of network storage for persistent operational data. Incorporating dual power-efficient P4 accelerators alongside substantial host resources, the server provides high resource density for deep learning model serving, video transcoding, image processing, and parallel compute pipelines without requiring high-tier training GPUs.
